input.quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: Section 4(c) is the operative licence-back of Contractor's Information embedded in the Works. It is royalty-free, perpetual and sublicensable (good), but it runs to "Company" only: our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not named, the licence is not stated to be irrevocable, and it is silent on transfer while § 10 (p0042) bars assignment or transfer without consent — leaving the licence arguably untransferable to a successor. That falls short of the preferred position (affiliates and contractors covered; paid-up licence perpetual and irrevocable; transferable to successors). Minimal redline adds affiliates and contractors, "irrevocable", and successor transferability without disturbing the rest of the grant.

proposal.summary: Extend § 4(c) licence to Company's affiliates and contractors, make it irrevocable, and permit transfer to a successor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the § 4(c) licence in Contractor's Information to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and made it irrevocable and transferable to a successor to our business, since our playbook requires that a paid-up licence be perpetual and irrevocable and usable by the group and service providers who actually operate the deliverables. If helpful, we can accept covering affiliates on written notice and transferability limited to an M&A successor.
